items.title: 1. The rest of the medical part: a whole version a round, or a line or two for each section?
items.where: Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue, P1
items.question:
Nine sections of the medical part read AI in the first batch and haven't been fixed: Call medics for, Who to Contact, Acute Medical and Neurological Rescue (these two paragraphs), My Brain Feels Damaged, Active Seizure's first part, MDMA's jaw tension, Chest Pain, Recent Oral Toxic Ingestion's charcoal and poison control paragraphs, and Serotonin Syndrome. How each option would go:

A: as now: one teaching card a round, and I carry what you do to the others and test them. Pro: you write one section a round. Con: my carries of your two medical versions read AI in all eight tries, so so far only the section you write turns Human.

B (my pick): next round, a short box for each of those sections, for a line or two of your own there: what you've seen, what you'd do, or what you think of the standard advice. I build each section around what you write and test it. Pro: the whole part in a round or two, and it's how my fixes went Human in the remedies, where something you wrote was near (Nausea Smoothers, DMSO, the ocean water). Con: untried on clinical text; a section that still reads AI comes back to you as a teaching card.

items.title: 2. Suspected Serotonin Syndrome: how to recognize it
items.your_version:
Recognizing serotonin toxicity

We can use the same Hunter criteria that clinicians use to diagnose serotonin syndrome. One or more of the these patterns makes the diagnosis more likely:
Spontaneous clonus: involuntary rhythmic muscle spasms, with no stimulation needed to set it off, would be one full pattern
Inducible clonus, spasms set off by stretching/flexing a muscle, plus agitation or sweating would be counted as one pattern altogether.
Ocular clonus (rapid involuntary eye movements) plus agitation or sweating, another pattern together. 
Another is tremor (shaking) along with hyperreflexia (abnormally brisk reflexes). 
Lastly, Hypertonia (muscular rigidity) with fever above 38°C (100.4°F), as well as ocular or inducible clonus.

So if you see any of these patterns, call medics.

items.my_version:
Clinicians often use the Hunter criteria. One or more of the following patterns makes serotonin toxicity more likely:

Spontaneous clonus: involuntary rhythmic muscle contractions and relaxations occurring without stimulation.

Inducible clonus plus agitation or sweating.

Ocular clonus plus agitation or sweating: rapid rhythmic involuntary eye movements.

Tremor plus hyperreflexia: shaking together with abnormally brisk reflexes.

Hypertonia plus fever: rigidity with temperature above 38°C (100.4°F), together with ocular or inducible clonus.

This is a recognition aid rather than a command to wait for every criterion before acting. Dangerous heat, rigidity, clonus, confusion, or rapid worsening deserves medical help.
